subject: Pricing check: $/1M tokens & dedicated GPU lanes — post-demo clarifications
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Cho <andrew.cho@acme.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-18T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing check: $/1M tokens & dedicated GPU lanes — post-demo clarifications

Hi Andrew — great demo this morning, thanks for taking the time. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can put together a tight pilot quote for Acme.

What we heard on the call:
- Primary workload: conversational assistant + occasional long-form summarization (99% chat, 1% batch summarize)
- Target service-level: 95th pct latency < 300ms for 512-token responses for interactive flows
- Expected steady-state concurrency: 120 concurrent users at peak (1.5k qps estimate across microservices) — you mentioned peaky bursts during business hours
- Initial monthly token target range: 250M–1.2B tokens depending on pilot success

What I need from you to finalize dedicated pricing options (we'll show 2–3 SKU bands):
1) A ballpark monthly token target (low / expected / high) you can commit for a 90-day pilot and for annual reserved lanes. Even ranges are fine.
2) Any firm preference on GPU family (you mentioned H100 for latency; you also said cost team is open to A100 if we show numbers).
3) Throughput target in RPS or tokens/sec for the interactive flow (helps us pick lane counts).

I'll loop Ben (SE) and Marissa (AE) into the next note so we can estimate per-1M-token unit economics for each reserved SKU and show throughput assumptions side-by-side.

Attachments: I'll attach a short SKU matrix once we agree targets.

Thanks,
Rachel
--
Rachel Kim
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
(rachel.kim@redwood.ai)

From: Andrew Cho <andrew.cho@acme.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-18T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing check: $/1M tokens & dedicated GPU lanes — post-demo clarifications

Thanks Rachel — quick answers below. I pulled these numbers with Lina from procurement.

1) Token target (monthly): low 300M, mid 650M, high 1.1B. Pilot we expect to run at mid (~650M) if the latency holds.
2) GPU preference: technical team prefers H100 for 95th pct latency on interactive prompts; procurement would like to see A100 pricing too.
3) Throughput target: for interactive flow we need ~18 tokens/sec per active session with bursts — mapping to peak concurrent 120 users -> ~2.2k tokens/sec sustained peak, bursts up to 4k tokens/sec for short windows.

Budget guidance: procurement indicated a target $/1M-tokens goal in the range $50–$120 depending on SLA and included observability (higher for stricter SLA + longer retention).

Lina (cc) will own paperwork once we have a clear pilot quote.

Cheers,
Andrew

Thanks Andrew — this is perfect. Ben, Marissa — looping you both to propose three reserved lanes with explicit $/1M-token math for Acme. I've sketched the options below (high level). See attached SKU matrix (redwood-dedicated-sku-matrix.xlsx) for the latency/throughput assumptions:

Option A — H100 focused (low-latency, smaller lane counts):
- Hardware: H100 80GB per node
- Reserved lanes: 4 nodes
- Estimated sustained throughput: ~4.5k tokens/sec across the pool (meets bursts when combined with autoscale to 5 nodes temporary)
- Monthly token capacity (sustained): 4.5k * 86,400 = 388.8M tokens/day -> but realistic effective tokens/month (70% utilization): ~8.16B (we'll price on committed ranges)
- Pilot friendly monthly targets: 300M / 650M / 1.1B mapped to fraction of capacity
- Suggested price band: $95 / $78 / $65 per 1M tokens (low/mid/high volume discounts) — rationale: higher-performance HW + 24/7 reserved availability + 95th pct latency SLO.

Option B — A100 focused (cost-optimized):
- Hardware: A100 80GB per node
- Reserved lanes: 6 nodes
- Estimated sustained throughput: ~3.6k tokens/sec across the pool
- Suggested price band: $72 / $58 / $48 per 1M tokens (low/mid/high) — rationale: lower unit cost at expense of slightly higher latency on 512-token responses.

Option C — Hybrid band (auto-fallback & cost mix):
- Hardware: 3x H100 + 4x A100 with smart routing (latency-critical traffic to H100)
- Effective sustained throughput: ~4.0k tokens/sec balanced
- Suggested price band: $85 / $70 / $56 per 1M tokens

Notes on math and assumptions (short):
- Our token definition aligns with the Gen API tokenization used in the demo; billing is per-inferred output + input tokens.
- We factor in KV/prefix caching where applicable (reduces effective billing for repeated prompts).
- Price/1M is computed from node-level operational cost + amortized HW + networking + observability + preferred margin.

Next steps:
- Ben: can you confirm the latency SLO mapping (95th pct at 512 tokens) for H100 vs A100 in the attached matrix and include estimated CPU/GPU hours per 1M tokens?
- Marissa: I'll need a 90-day pilot quote for the mid (650M) and a longer-term reserved quote for 12 months at the mid/high tiers. Include pilot discounts and onboarding credits.
- Andrew/Lina: if the $/1M bands look directionally OK, we'll circulate a draft MPA and a pilot PO.

Thanks — Rachel

--
Rachel Kim
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Pricing check: $/1M tokens & dedicated GPU lanes — post-demo clarifications

Adding the SE view and a quick cost-per-1M breakdown (draft numbers; see attached workbook):

Assumptions used for these calculations:
- Token throughput mapping: 1 token ~= 0.005 compute units (avg across prompt distribution)
- H100 node amortized cost + infra + ops = $25k/mo (example for reserved pricing)
- A100 node amortized cost + infra + ops = $18k/mo

Rough cost math (simplified):
- H100 4-node reserved pool: cost=4*$25k=$100k/mo -> if you commit 650M tokens, cost-per-1M = $100k / 650 = ~$153 (gross) -> after standard reserved discount + margin we present $78 as Rachel suggested (net to customer).
- A100 6-node reserved pool: cost=6*$18k=$108k/mo -> /650M = ~$166 gross -> after discount we present $58.

Important SE notes:
- The gross numbers are intentionally conservative at the node-cost level; the customer-facing $/1M includes utilization improvements (prefix caching) and multi-tenant opportunistic bursts on dedicated lanes in off-peak windows (we can lower effective $/1M).
- If Acme can commit to a minimum monthly of 1.1B we can materially lower the presented price band (see hybrid option).
- For SLA: H100 baseline is more predictable for 95th pct latency; A100 will meet median easily but 95th will be ~15–30% higher depending on sequence length and concurrency.

Action: I've updated the attached SKU matrix (redwood-dedicated-sku-matrix.xlsx) with per-node hours/1M token estimates and toggles for prefix cache effectiveness. Please review and I'll bake into a formal pilot quote PDF (draft-mpa-acme-2027-07-20.pdf).

-ben

- Preferred pilot HW: H100 (tech) but include A100 alternate pricing for procurement review
- Proposed pilot price (from our draft): $78 per 1M tokens for H100 pilot band (650M); $58 per 1M tokens for A100 alternative
- Attachments circulated: SKU matrix + draft MPA (redwood-dedicated-sku-matrix.xlsx, draft-mpa-acme-2027-07-20.pdf)

Immediate asks for Acme:
1) Lina: please confirm procurement's preferred PO terms (net-30? any invoicing requirements) and whether a PO for the 90-day pilot at 650M tokens is possible this week.
2) Andrew: confirm you want H100 as the pilot baseline; if yes we'll reserve a 4-node H100 lane for the pilot start date target (2027-08-02) and schedule a final baseline performance test next week.

If we have the PO & H100 confirmation by Thu 2027-07-22 EOD we can lock the pilot start for Aug 2, include a one-week ramp window, and commit to the latency SLO in the pilot MPA.

Thanks — looking forward to moving to PO stage.

Rachel
